previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, chronic diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and diabetes was admitted for acute respiratory distress following an episode of palpitations and worsening shortness of breath. She had been discharged the prior day after an admission for dialysis-related chest pain and hypotension. This admission was attributed to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with pulmonary edema, likely triggered by a tachyarrhythmia. She was treated with intravenous nitroglycerin, BiPap support, and hemodialysis with removal of 3.5 liters of fluid. Her heart rate was controlled with rate-limiting medications, and her warfarin dose was temporarily increased due to a low INR. She stabilized on room air, had no further symptoms, and was discharged home with instructions on weight monitoring, fluid and sodium restriction, and continuation of dialysis and medications. Follow-up was arranged through her dialysis clinic for INR monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
#Hypotension - Attributed to a combination of antihypertensive 
medications and a recent increase in the target dry weight for 
hemodialysis. Resolved with fluid resuscitation. 
Antihypertensive medications were gradually added and blood 
pressure and heart rate were well-controlled with metoprolol 
12.5 BID (reduced from an outpatient dose of Toprol XL 100 mg) 
and verapamil 40 mg TID (reduced from an outpatient dose of 80 
mg TID) upon discharge. Lisinopril, valsartan, and isosorbide 
mononitrate were discontinued. 
.
#Chronic diastolic heart failure - Positive cardiac biomarkers 
were attributed to subendocardial ischemia in the setting of 
hypotension and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate 
given the patient's known LVH and LVOT. Acute coronary syndrome 
was felt to be unlikely given a normal cardiac catheterization ___ 
year prior to admission and the absence of a new wall motion 
abnormality on TTE. She was seen in consultation by cardiology 
who agreed with this assessment and recommended continuing 
medical management with blood pressure and rate control, 
aspirin, and statin therapy.  She will be seen in close follow 
up by her cardiologist the week after discharge.
.
#Chronic kidney disease stage V - Hemodialysis was continued, 
without recurrent episodes of hypotension. Calcium acetate was 
discontinued due to hypophosphatemia.
.
#Atrial fibrillation - Rate was well-controlled despite reduced 
doses of metoprolol and verapamil. Continued amiodarone.
.
#Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus - Blood sugars were 
well-controlled with basal and sliding scale insulin.
.
#Dyslipidemia - Continued simvastatin.
